name: 1912 Prairie Avenue (the Moulton/Lowden house): the brick barn on the alley under a hip and deck, K12

function.note: Sheet 28 of the 1911 Sanborn letters the two-storey brick building on the alley behind 1912 BARN, the sheet's word for a stable (as at 1834 and 1906). The T-1841 sheet census (row s28-1912-rear) backcasts the building to 1904, and this record builds it as the house's stable and coach house: two carriage bays, a loft hatch with its hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. INFERRED from the 1911 label carried back to 1904; no source read names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

research_note: T-1935 refines the district draft (T-2329) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the sixth of the package's seven alley buildings on the west side of Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th, after 1816's, 1824's, 1834's, 1900's and 1906's. The sheet census (census row s28-1912-rear, trace s28fp-1912-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 28 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle (which stood a 9.25 x 16.25 m block under a gable): the sheet draws one building 10.442 m deep and 17.531 m along the alley on the alley line, its north wall on the line it shares with 1906's one-storey range (row 4532.80, the reading 1906's record takes) and its south wall on the line it shares with the one-storey building south of it. Inside its walls the sheet draws a dashed deck line with a diagonal into every corner, the plan of a hip cut off at a deck, so this one is built under the kit's new hip_deck roof and not its gable, and with no party wall, since both neighbours are a storey lower. Robinson's 1886 atlas (plate 10) stops at 18th Street, so nothing read here dates the building before 1911. Neither picture the T-1935 image gate names for it shows it: Clark's c. 1905 street view north from 1936 shows the house fronts on Prairie Avenue, and the New Chicago Album's 1883 vignette of B. F. Moulton's house its front alone; no camera is solved.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Robinson's 1886 plate 10 stops at 18th Street, and nothing else read dates this one, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json): local E 1339.971, N -3395.682, plus the datum origin. The bearing is the parcel's own (its north and south lines run at 0.617 degrees north of east), so the building's ends lie along the lot lines.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is pixel (561.61, 4706.175) of the committed sheet 28 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (column 561.61 at its middle row) to its east wall line (768.42, 768.41, 768.19 and 767.60 at the same four row bands; 768.14 at the middle row), 206.53 pixels at the sheet's 0.050558 m a pixel, 10.442 m deep, and from its north wall line (row 4532.80, the line it shares with 1906's one-storey range, which 1906's record reads there; read here at columns 600-640 and 680-720 as 4532.60 and 4534.08) to its south one (4879.55: 4878.83 and 4880.26), 346.75 pixels, 17.531 m along the alley. It is one rectangle: no piece, wing or open strip. The sheet writes '12' across both end lines, read as the walls' thickness in inches; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls. The lot line the parcel reads at the street (row 4546.0) is not this building's: the barn stands on its own lines, 0.67 m north of it, as the sheet draws.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-west corner, inside the dashed deck line's corner. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave; the hip rises over that to the deck, 1.33 m above the eave line, and holds no storey.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with '12' across the north and south wall lines.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick, the roof's plan and the one window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1912-barn-1935. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, a dashed line inside the walls with a diagonal from each of its corners into the building's corners, which is the sheet's plan of a roof's deck and hips (as it is read on 1912's own house and on 1936's: T-2934), and one of the key's window marks on the alley wall, a cross with a dot for each storey (the sign 1816's, 1824's, 1834's, 1900's and 1906's alley walls carry), 8.251 m south of the north wall line (row 4696.0). It letters the building BARN. Unlike the package's other five, it is roofed as the sheet draws it and not with the kit's gable: roof_form 'hip_deck' (added to the kit by this ticket), four walls level at the eave and a hip from every corner rising at the kit's 40 degrees to a flat deck. The dashed line stands 1.6 m in from the north wall line (row 4564.5), 1.4 m in from the east (column 740.5) and 1.77 m in from the south (row 4844.5), read by mean darkness profile because it is dashed; no dashed run is drawn along the alley wall, but both of the alley-side diagonals end where an equal inset puts the deck's west corners, so the deck is built 1.59 m in on all four sides (the three readings' mean; a hand-drawn dash is not read finer than that) and its edge stands 1.33 m over the eave line. Its felt covering is the kit's. There is no party wall: the buildings either side are one storey (1906's range north, the '1' south), so the barn's two storeys stand clear above both, and its end walls are plain brick without openings, which the sheet does not mark on them. The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s counts on the alley wall from the north wall's outer face, and on the yard wall from the south wall's). The rest of the alley wall is the kit's laid out for 17.5 m: two carriage bays 3.0 m clear, the loft hatch and hoist over the northern one and a loft sash over the other, a man door between the northern bay and the mark, and a stable sash and loft sash toward the south end. The yard wall has a door where the walk to the house meets it and five stable sash with loft sash over them. The workyard is paved from the yard door 7.901 m east to the west face of the house's two-storey brick rear range (sheet column 924.25, rows 4686.4-4822.06), the walk on that range's middle, 2.43 m south of the building's. The small ring the sheet draws inside the building's south-west corner, as it does inside 1824's, 1900's and 1906's, is the key's slate-or-tin roof sign: the kit's slate stands on the hips, and the deck is felted.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above), and its roof's plan the sheet's; its openings, the roof's pitch and covering, and the workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED except where the window mark places a sash. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.
